claim: The engineered surface flexibility will absorb pressure fluctuations and reduce turbulent stress transfer, decreasing drag by 3-6% while maintaining structural integrity
mechanism: The HDPE micro-structured surface will have localized flexibility that allows it to deform under hydrodynamic loading, absorbing pressure fluctuations and reducing the transfer of turbulent stresses to the pipe wall. This mimics the skin flexibility of sharks that helps reduce drag by dampening near-wall turbulence.
evidence: Shark skin flexibility contributes to drag reduction by absorbing pressure fluctuations
Flexible polymer surfaces have shown drag reduction in some applications
assumptions: The HDPE material maintains flexibility at operating temperatures
The micro-structure doesn't compromise the material's structural integrity
The surface deformation doesn't lead to increased roughness over time
novelty_rationale: Focuses on the material flexibility aspect of shark skin rather than just surface topology, applying it to pipe flow
testability: Can be tested by measuring pressure fluctuations along the pipe wall and comparing pressure drop between flexible and rigid micro-structured surfaces
falsifier: If pressure fluctuations are not reduced or if the flexible surface shows increased drag compared to rigid micro-structures
